comment: dr boone is sweet and passionate but i wouldnt take her again. her tests have a cheat sheet but it doesn't matter because you dont use it on the tests since all her questions are subjective and mcq so theres barely any half credit. her labs are extremely hard to understand and she grades them very harshly.
She is clear about her expectations, classes can be a little boring but she does activities to make it more interesting. Projects were fun and she is a fair grader.

Prof. Boone is super sweet and very knowledgeable on Environmental Studies. There were some long textbook homework's, but easy work. Her exams are a bit tricky, but she let us use a page of notes while taking them to back up your answers. The final project was a lot of fun as a graphic designer conveying a message about environmental sustainability
very easy class, spent very little time outside of class on work. class can be boring and quizzes are sometimes confusing, would just recommend taking notes. you can use cheat sheet on the quizzes

This class was super chill and Emily is very nice. On 2/3  of the quizzes (basically tests), we were allowed a cheat sheet, and they were pretty straightforward anyway. Lecture heavy, but if you take good notes you should be totally fine. Not much homework and no final just a final project and v short presentation.

I've taken two of her classes and loved both! She's super chill, as long as you take good notes and don't forget the online textbook homework you should do well, and she's always willing to talk about things outside of class. I don't agree at all with people saying her tests are hard, the application is usually related to in-class examples.

Emily is amazing!  There are always chances for extra credit after the exam which will increase your grade. She is very clear on her criteria. There is not much work to do outside of the classroom. People say her exams are hard but I disagree. They are open note, and are more about your overall understanding.

Emily is a great person and a blast to have a lab with. She makes it easy to do well in the labs, and we do some pretty cool things, like tagging turtles. BUT her tests are super hard and all based on integration (open note), and the notes barely help. Still can achieve an A easily, but tests are def hard.

Emily was such a caring and understanding teacher. Very accesible inside and outside of class and understanding of absences. Very homework heavy in the beginning but workload gets lighter towards the end of the semester. Every lab has extremely clear grading criteria so easy to get As on. Tests are very difficult to do well on, but are open note.

This class is more than worthwhile. I appreciated the online program to learn about ecology and biology. Even as a 3rd year bio major I learned a fair amount. A big plus is most assignments can be done well in advance, letting you control your time. Emily is hilarious and also very good at handling sensitive topics if you reach out.

My favorite class last semester by far. The lectures were long but Professor Boone's sarcastic comments pulled me through it. She sets extremely clear expectations for tests (which are all open note!) and lab reports. If you follow the rubric she give, you will get an A. She is very willing to help all students, class related or not. Love.

Emily was a great professor! She is always willing to help and was always available outside of class when you needed it. Labs were SO FUN! p.s we went into the lake and held turtles. We only had three tests, which were hard but doable and you can do a test wrapper and get points back. Would definitely recommend her class!

Emily is so amazing if you get to know her. She really cares about her students and the labs you do are really fun. The class is super collaborative and there are only 3 big tests. The questions can be a little confusing but she lets you redo some questions.

Only three open note exams. Very accessible outside of class if you need help. The class starts off heavy and then chills down towards the end of the year. Probably the easiest bio 199 class you can take. Cares about her students

Professor Boone did a good job teaching an intro level bio course. While lectures might sometimes be boring or not seem immediately relevant, things tie together more and more as the semester moves on. Definitely go to office hours to get feedback on lab reports. Not an easy nor a guaranteed A, but you'll get an A if you put the time and effort in.

I did not like this class at first, but it really grew on me. Tests are open book and she grades projects/essays very easy. Emily is super kind and helpful. Definitely go to her office hours because she likes you a lot better if you do!

Emily is a pretty good professor, is always available for questions, and the tests were all open note. Her lectures are mostly just her reading off the slides but each class she incorporated some sort of game or real world example to keep us engaged. Overall not a hard class, material is easy

Sooooo boring. We did SimUText for homework which was not relevant to what we talked about in class. I missed the deadline for one of the SimUText's and it tanked my grade because they're weighed so heavily. And the quizzes have the stupidest questions, impossible to prepare for them. She always seemed annoyed with me when I would speak to her.

Intro to ES is an easy course that is fairly interesting (sometimes the content felt oversimplified). Emily is super kind/accessible and clearly wants students to do well in her class. She drops your lowest quiz grade and the quizzes were open note. If you are planning on majoring in ES, definitely take this class with Emily!

I enjoyed Intro to Environmental Studies with Emily, the class is very easy, and quizzes are open note. She lets you drop one of your quizzes at the end of the semester, and really helps you get a good grade. She is always available outside of class and responds to emails quickly.

6 quizzes and they were in total 60% of our final grade. They were extremely difficult and most people had a hard time getting above a C on each of them. SHe was nice, but never really seemed happy and sometimes it seemed like our classes were filled with busy work that was kind of pointless. Last project we had to present in front of the class

Dr. Boone didn't seem very interested in the lectures she gave and just read off the screen. Talking to her one-on-one is better than just seeing her lectures. We had quizzes, which were harder than I had expected, since it was an intro class. The class project was good and each week was helpful in learning new subjects for the major. Very nice!

Professor Boone is nice enough, but her classes are fairly boring. Usually just note taking from slides. Her quizzes should be easy as the material is not hard, but the way the questions are worded set you up to do poorly. It is not a hard class, but it is hard to get a really good grade in it. Also, a decent amount of reading for homework.
A lot of writing criteria, unclear lectures that make it very confusing to understand, monotone voice.
She grades ridiculously hard and lowkey judges you if you ask a question or are confused about something. Dont take her.
Worst teacher ever. Exams are not actually about biology and instead care more about spelling errors and word choice. DONT TAKE HER

Shes a very tough grader and can be hard to reach outside of class. Even if you try to learn the subject, it feels as if theres no point because its nearly impossible to do well. She teaches at a very fast pace and expects you to memorize so many things within such a short span of time.

She knows her subject very well but her tests are EXTREMELY hard. Every test she basically failed the whole class and she needed to curve it every time. The tests had questions not related to the study guide at all and were beyond hard. Even if you study, its nearly impossible to get a good grade.

Emily is great. She cares a lot and is fair to students. She does small group discussions and activities along with lectures to keep everyone engaged. She also drops lowest quiz and discussion board posts. She tries to cater to different learning styles. Tips: Get to know her outside of class & show engagement w material & talk in class discussions

Most assignments were just readings that'd be discussed in the next class. We had quizzes every 2 weeks or so, but they weren't too difficult. We used SimuText as our "textbook", but other than that, we didn't have a physical textbook. Very chill and informative!

Emily is a decent professor. She is fairly interesting and you can tell she enjoys the subject, although she hides it well sometimes. Many students describe her as a bit standoffish in class at times, but having interacted with her outside of class I know she's not always like this. She isn't really one for small talk. I woudn't avoid taking her.

Emily Boone is a great professor for BIO199. She definitely takes her class seriously and wants all students to work hard and participate, but she can still joke around and her lectures are not dry. If you like Biology and pay attention in class, it is not hard to get a good grade.

Emily is a great professor that clearly knows a lot about and is passionate about marine biology. Labs and trips are especially helpful because they give you a chance to see what you're learning in a real setting. She also teaches a lot of helpful statistics and excel stuff that is great for students who haven't taken stats before.

She's really nice and chill. As long as youre earnest and do your work, you will be rewarded for your efforts. You can always ask her for feedback and she is willing to listen and help. PowerPoints were usually very helpful and make it convenient to take notes. She also is clear on what she wants, and gives rubrics for lab reports. Would recommend!

Emily is definitely my favorite professor at UR. When you first meet her she can definitely be standoffish, but once you get to know her she's funny and very willing to help. In class, there are a lot of lecture for ENV 201 and she lectures from a powerpoint which are only useful if you take notes. I highly recommend her BIO 199 which I also took
After this class, I don't like anything about macro-biology : )
Emily made the lab that came with this course so much fun. The hands on experience really helped to drive home what was being learned in the course. She is laid back and really knew her stuff.

She gives very specific guidelines on writing a lab report. If you follow her guidelines, you'll get a good grade. She is willing to get to know her students and offered help in class and outside class when asked.

It's not even that she is a tough grader. The grading style is based on a rubric. You can end up with a C on an otherwise well-written lab because you missed a few minor things on the checklist. Very frustrating. Would not take again.

I feel like she doesn't have a reason to grade as harshly as she does. She kind've seemed unenthusiastic about her job, which makes sense since the lab is extremely boring for this course. Writing lab reports was painful because she doesn't tell you what she wants and is way too picky about grading. She also goes by her first name, which is weird.

I really did not put a whole lot of effort into the class as there were very few readings due. I know a lot of people didn't do very well, but as long as you pay attention in class, you will be fine. She doesn't pull surprises on tests, but she expects you to apply what you learn.  Overall, I learned a lot, got a good grade, and enjoyed the class.
I used to love Environmental Studies. Now I hate it.

She is a horrible lab instructor - I have no idea why she is in charge of Physiology Labs. She is an extremely hard and unfair grader. Her grading standards are ridiculous and incorrect. She doesn't abide by the typical "rules" of how to write a proper lab report of journal article.

She is not too bad outside of class, but I don't think she really cares about lab.  She seems bitter about not getting into Vet school.  It seems as though she takes this bitterness out on everyone else going pre-med or pre-vet by being a really harsh grader.
She's a nice lady. However, I wouldn't necessarily call her enthusiastic, and she's a hard grader.
Emily is great!  Her grading is fair as long as you follow the directions.  You'll be fine as long as you submit a draft of your papers for her to read.
EBOONE IS AWESOME! Belize 2005
Emily is very nice outside of the classroom, but she grades very harshly and almost looks for ways to give you a bad grade.  Try to get on her good side and you may do well.
Emily is a nice person.  I found her grading style especially in biology 203 to be overly critical.  Her lectures are boring but outside of the class room I liked her much better.

She admits she doesn't want to be a lab instructor and it shows. If you care about science, especially the scientific method, get a different lab instructor. Her lack of commitment hurts the class. Not to mention she repeats what you heard in lecture verbatem. Her lab is the reason for caffeine.

Quarky sense of humor amd her ability to relate to her students make her a good lab teacher.  She grades easily, especially if you turn in a draft. Beware of her in lab lecture periods though, they can bore you to death.  Otherwise she's worth taking.
